newsitem.title: ITALY: EU commissioner attacks Alitalia plan.
newsitem.headline: EU commissioner attacks Alitalia plan.

text.p: European Union Commissioner Neil Kinnock has told Italy's government that a plan to recapitalise loss-making state airline Alitalia has major shortcomings, an Italian business newspaper said on Wednesday.

Milan financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore said in a report from Brussels that Kinnock had told the company and Italy's Transport ministry that the government's planned three trillion lire capital injection would not generate a sufficiently high return.

In a letter sent on April 18, Kinnock described the Alitalia plan as "more prudent and more realistic than the preceding one" but said it was subject to "significant commercial risks" the report said.

The government controls Alitalia through state holding company IRI which owns 87 percent of the airline's stock. Kinnock said in order to obtain approval of the recapitalisation plan Alitalia had two options.

The first was for Alitalia to make the plan commercially viable by imposing greater sacrifices on the business, ranging from a cut in unit labour costs to reductions in fleet size and planned investments.

However, Kinnock said if Alitalia was unable to carry through these changes swiftly the recapitalisation plan should be put forward by Alitalia for approval as straightforward state aid, Il Sole reported.
Il Sole said no immediate reaction to the letter had been forthcoming from Alitalia chairman Domenico Cempella or Transport Minister Claudio Burlando.
Kinnock's letter said the Cempella restructuring plan would generate a 15 percent return, well below the 30 percent return considered acceptable by the EU Commission.

The Commission expressed objections to Alitalia's inclusion of 1.2 trillion lire in short term credits received from IRI in 1996 in its forecast of the company's net worth in the year 2000, the newspaper said.
